# Kyoto 3-Day Budget Trip Plan

A relaxed Kyoto itinerary for 2 adults, centered on temples, local food, and one low-cost cultural activity each day. I’ve kept the pace to stay under about 12,000 steps per day by grouping sights into compact areas and using short transit rides where helpful.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Costs

### Day 1 — Higashiyama Classics + Gion Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Ninenzaka; start early to avoid crowds and heat.
- Afternoon: Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and a slow walk through Gion.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park, and a slow walk through Gion, Kyoto, Japan
- Cultural activity: Free or low-cost temple grounds and shrine exploration; optional small donation or entry fee.
- Food: Matcha sweets, yudofu lunch, and a casual izakaya dinner.
- Walking target: About 9,000–11,000 steps.

### Day 2 — Arashiyama + Western Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji area, and Togetsukyo Bridge.
- Afternoon: Okochi Sanso garden or a riverside café break, then a short train ride back.
- Cultural activity: Garden visit or a small tea-house stop with a traditional atmosphere.
- Food: Tofu lunch in Arashiyama and a simple noodle or curry dinner back in central Kyoto.
- Walking target: About 8,000–10,500 steps.

### Day 3 — Central Kyoto Temples + Craft Experience
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- Morning: Nijo Castle or Kyoto Imperial Palace area, depending on your pace preference.
- Afternoon: Nishiki Market for snacks, then a low-cost cultural activity such as a tea ceremony, kimono-accessory workshop, or small craft class.
- Cultural activity: Tea ceremony or compact hands-on workshop.
- Food: Market tasting lunch, then a relaxed kaiseki-lite or set-meal dinner.
- Walking target: About 7,000–10,500 steps.

## Estimated Budget for 2 Adults

| Item | Estimated Cost (USD) | Estimated Cost (JPY) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hotels, 3 nights | 420–540 | 63,000–81,000 |
| Local transit | 35–60 | 5,250–9,000 |
| Temple/shrine entries | 30–70 | 4,500–10,500 |
| Low-cost cultural activities | 40–90 | 6,000–13,500 |
| Food and drinks | 280–380 | 42,000–57,000 |
| Miscellaneous buffer | 60–90 | 9,000–13,500 |
| Total | **865–1,230** | **129,750–184,500** |

## Best Fit for Your Budget

### Recommended spending profile
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-rupee.svg
- **Comfortable budget target:** about **USD 950–1,100** total for 2 adults.
- This leaves room for one nicer dinner or a better hotel without pushing too close to the ceiling.
- To stay under **USD 1,200**, keep hotels in the mid-range and choose one paid cultural activity per day max.

### Step-count control
- Group Day 1 around Higashiyama/Gion.
- Use the Sagano area on Day 2 without adding extra side detours.
- Keep Day 3 centered on central Kyoto and Nishiki Market.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Keep Day 3 centered on central Kyoto and Nishiki Market, Kyoto, Japan
- If you want to reduce walking further, use buses or short taxi rides between clustered sights.
